GrandMaster Guide is a complete chess school in your pocket, made by Zorix. It teaches chess step by step from the very first move with 322 interactive lessons in seven courses, explains every move with a personal coach in text and voice, lets you play against 20 levels of the engine, train with puzzles, build your own positions and analyse any game with Stockfish 19, the strongest chess engine in the world. Everything runs on your phone, completely offline: no account and no internet connection are needed, and nothing leaves your device.
Zorix engine core: based on Stockfish 19 (GNU GPL v3)
Coach voices: sherpa-onnx (Apache 2.0), the Piper voices “ganji” for Persian and Kurdish (MIT, CC0 data) and “ljspeech” for English (MIT, public-domain data), and espeak-ng (GPL v3)

string-array.name: help_analysis
string-array.item: What it is|The main board of the app. Play moves for both sides or set up any position, and let the engine — Stockfish 19, the strongest chess engine in the world, running on your phone — find the best move and evaluate the position.
Moving pieces|Tap a piece and then a square, or drag it. Dots show the legal squares. When a pawn reaches the last rank you choose the new piece (queen, rook, bishop or knight).
Best move|Tap “Best move”: the engine thinks for the time chosen in Settings and draws its move as a green arrow, with the evaluation and the expected continuation. Tap the suggestion to play it.
Live analysis|The chart button at the top turns continuous analysis on: up to three candidate moves (green, blue and orange arrows), the evaluation bar beside the board and the search depth.

Reading the evaluation|+1.00 means White is better by about one pawn; −2.50 means Black is better by two and a half pawns; #3 means mate in 3 moves. The bar next to the board shows the same thing at a glance.
Coach|With the coach switched on, every move you play is rated (best, excellent, good, inaccuracy, mistake, blunder…) and explained, together with the better move.
Moves, undo and redo|Tap any move in the list under the board to jump to it. The undo and redo buttons step backwards and forwards through the game.
Build a puzzle|The pencil button opens the puzzle builder: set up any position and analyse it.
Menu ⋮|New game, build a position, load or copy FEN (a one-line text description of a position), copy or share the game as PGN (the standard game format), and About.

string-array.name: help_builder
string-array.item: What it is|Set up any position — a puzzle from a book, a moment from your own game or an idea you want to test — and let the engine analyse it.
The kings|Both kings are always on the board and cannot be removed. To move a king, choose it in the palette (the outlined king) and tap the new square.

Placing pieces|Choose a piece and tap squares to place it; tap the same piece again to remove it, or use the eraser. You can use any number of each piece — up to 32 pieces in total, the most the engine can evaluate.

Rules that still apply|Pawns cannot stand on the first or last rank. The side that is not to move must not be in check, because such a position can never happen; change the side to move or move the pieces.
Side to move and castling|Choose who is to move. Castling can be allowed only while the king and that rook stand on their starting squares.
Analyse|“Analyse position” opens it on the analysis board, where Best move and live analysis work as usual. The flip button turns the board around.

string-array.name: help_play
string-array.item: Play against Zorix|20 levels, from a complete beginner (level 1) to the full strength of the engine (level 20). The lower levels make human-like mistakes on purpose; the higher ones play like club players, masters and grandmasters.
Choosing a level|The level marked “Recommended” suits you best, but you can play any level. Winning earns stars on that level — three stars for a win without hints or take-backs.
Colour|Before the game choose White, Black or a random colour.

string-array.name: help_game
string-array.item: During the game|Make your moves on the board and Zorix answers. The coach rates and explains every move you play. With “Explain Zorix\'s moves” switched on in Settings, it also explains the opponent\'s moves and warns you about its threats.
Hint|Shows the best move as an arrow with its explanation. A win with hints earns fewer stars.
Take back|Takes back your last move together with Zorix\'s reply.
Draw and resign|Offer a draw — Zorix accepts only when the position is really equal — or resign the game.
Listen|The speaker button reads the last explanation aloud.
After the game|Open the review to see your accuracy, the key moments and to find the better moves yourself.

string-array.name: help_review
string-array.item: Game review|Every move of the game is rated. Accuracy (0–100%) shows how close the moves were to the engine\'s best moves.
Key moments|The moves that changed the game most: mistakes, missed chances and great moves. Tap one to see it on the board with its explanation.
Try again|At a mistake, tap “Try again” and find the better move yourself.

string-array.name: help_learn
string-array.item: Courses|Seven courses take you from zero to an advanced level: Chess Basics, Chess Understanding, Checkmate Patterns, Tactics, Endgames, Openings and Strategy. If you are new to chess, start with Chess Basics.
Step by step|Lessons open one after another: finishing a lesson opens the next one. Each lesson gives up to three stars.
Kinds of exercises|Explanations with diagrams, moving a piece to stars, captures, quizzes, finding the best move, puzzles, mate in N, playing opening lines and playing endgames out against Zorix.

string-array.name: help_lesson
string-array.item: Steps|Read or listen to the explanation, then solve each exercise. The bar at the top shows your progress through the lesson.
Hint and solution|Hint highlights the piece to move. Solution shows the answer and explains it, but counts as a mistake.

Voice|Reads explanations aloud with natural voices built into the app, with no internet needed: an English voice, a Persian voice and a native Sorani Kurdish voice. Tap the speaker icon to hear an explanation again.
Stars|No mistakes: three stars. One or two mistakes: two stars. More: one star. You can repeat any lesson to improve your result.

string-array.name: help_puzzles
string-array.item: Puzzles|Real positions with one winning solution. Find the best move for the side to move; when the opponent answers, keep going until the puzzle is solved.
Modes|Practice: the puzzles get harder as you solve them. Streak: solve as many as you can in a row — one mistake ends the streak. Themes: practise one idea, such as forks, pins or mates.
Hint and solution|Hint highlights the piece to move; Solution plays the answer and explains it.
Your own puzzles|The pencil button opens the builder: set up any position and analyse it.

string-array.name: help_settings
string-array.item: Profile|The name the coach uses when it talks to you.
Appearance|Zorix: dark style in black and red. Sky: light style in white and sky blue.
Language|Persian, Kurdish (Sorani) or English. “System” follows the phone\'s language.
Coach|Rates and explains every move you play on the analysis board.

Voice|Reads explanations aloud with natural voices built into the app, with no internet needed: an English voice, a Persian voice, and for Kurdish the same voice speaking from Kurdish pronunciation rules, so the Kurdish text itself is read. Tap the speaker icon to hear an explanation again.

Think time|How long the engine thinks when you tap Best move, from 0.5 to 30 seconds. Longer means deeper and more accurate, but slower. 2–5 seconds is enough for most positions; use 10–30 seconds for difficult endgames or sharp tactics.
CPU threads|How many processor cores the engine uses at the same time. More threads analyse faster and deeper, but use more battery and warm the phone. A good choice is the number of cores minus one.

Memory (hash)|Memory for the engine\'s table of positions it has already analysed, so it does not calculate them twice. 64 MB suits most phones; 128–256 MB helps long thinking times on phones with plenty of RAM.
Lines|How many candidate moves live analysis shows (1–3). More lines give more information, but each one is calculated a little less deeply.
Depth|The depth shown during analysis is how many half-moves ahead the engine has calculated. It grows with the think time and the number of threads; depth 20 or more is very strong.
Board|Board colours, coordinates (a–h, 1–8), dots for legal moves, arrows, move animations and vibration.
